expl.summary: This formula has no jet-mass observable among its if-statements, and it reaches a validation accuracy of 81.0%. The mass information comes back through e2_sq, girth2 and width, which all order jets by (mass / pT) squared (identical rank correlations with mass_over_sum_pt_sq in the pack), combined with thresholds on the total pT. Several neurons are bands in these quantities: neuron 0 is highest for e2_sq between 0.0062 and 0.0079, neuron 7 for e2_sq and girth2 between 0.0079 and 0.0096 at total pT above 1167 GeV, neuron 14 for girth2 above 0.0082 with e2_sq below 0.020, and neuron 12 applies a girth2 threshold that is tighter above 908 GeV total pT than below it. As a result, neurons 0, 8, 9 and 12 follow the jet mass itself (rank correlations -0.647, 0.685, -0.633, -0.688) although mass never appears in a test. The W and Z scores are separated mainly by these bands: the W score adds neuron 0 (+11%), which the Z score subtracts (-21%), and the Z score adds neuron 7 (+9%), which the W score subtracts (-6%). Both boson scores subtract the large-girth2 neuron 8 (-24% and -26%) and add neuron 5 (pT held in the 50 hardest particles, e2_sq below 0.0079; +15% and +17%). The t score adds the large-girth neuron 10 (+29%) and subtracts neuron 13 (-35%), which is high for jets above 908 GeV total pT that do not spread pT to large girth2; tops average 0.56 on it against 1.44-2.07 for the other classes. Gluon and quark scores both add the narrow-jet neuron 9 (+14% and +25%) and subtract neuron 4 (compact core with low D2; -16% and -31%); they are separated by particle multiplicity: neuron 1 (many particles, pT beyond the 40-50 hardest) gives 46% of the g score and subtracts 21% from the q score, and freezing it costs 12.1 points of accuracy, by far the most of any neuron.

0.title: e2_sq in a narrow band (0.0062-0.0079) at moderate total pT
0.measures: Its strongest term adds for e2_sq < 0.00787, a second adds for e2_sq < 0.00694, while e2_sq < 0.00617 and e2_sq < 0.00961 push it down, so it is largest for e2_sq between about 0.0062 and 0.0079. It is also raised for pT of the 40 hardest particles > 859 GeV and for pT of the 30 hardest < 1192 GeV, and lowered for total pT > 1002 GeV, so the e2_sq band is read at a moderate pT; small girth2 (< 0.0082) raises it. It falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.647), e2_sq, width and girth2 (-0.616 each). W jets sit clearly highest (1.65, zero for only 2.0% of them), then quarks (0.80), gluons (0.34), Z (0.27) and tops (0.10, zero for 88.8%); it is zero for 41.3% of Z jets and 53.2% of gluons.
0.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-21%), the largest-but-one input of the Z score, so it is one of the two neurons that separate W from Z jets. It raises the t score slightly (+2%) and does not enter the g or q scores. Freezing it costs 2.22 points of accuracy.

1.title: high particle multiplicity, pT spread beyond the 40-50 hardest particles
1.measures: Raised for total pT > 972 GeV and log of total pT > 6.91, but lowered for pT of the 50 hardest particles > 934 GeV, so it counts the pT carried by particles beyond the 50 hardest; it is further raised for more than 38 particles and for a softest particle with pT share < 0.00145, and lowered for softest-particle pT < 2.28 GeV. It follows the number of particles (rank correlation 0.653), the number above 1 GeV (0.632) and falls with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles (-0.614). Gluons sit far above the rest (5.88, AUC 0.92), then tops (2.91), quarks (2.23), Z (1.74) and W (1.58); it is non-zero for 99.8% of gluons and zero for 8.8% of quarks and 11.3% of W jets. Its values reach 9.56, the widest range of all neurons.
1.role: It raises the g score (+46%, its largest input) and lowers the q score (-21%), so it is the main input that separates gluon from quark jets. It does not enter the W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 12.14 points of accuracy, the largest drop of any neuron.

2.title: high total pT, moderate girth (neither very narrow nor very wide)
2.measures: Pushed down for LHA > 0.372 (its strongest term) and for girth2 < 0.00694, pushed up for girth2 of the 50 hardest particles < 0.00635, for lam1 < 0.0117 and for total pT > 1008 GeV; it follows the total pT (rank correlation 0.525). Gluons sit highest (0.62), then Z (0.25), W (0.20), quarks (0.13) and tops (0.04); it is zero for 34.5% of gluons, 74.3% of quarks and 88.2% of tops.
2.role: It lowers the Z score slightly (-2%) and does not enter the g, q, W or t scores (its share in the q score is +1%). Freezing it changes accuracy by -0.02 points.

3.title: few particles, little radiation at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, small minor axis
3.measures: Raised for fewer than 46 particles (its strongest term), girth2 of the 40 hardest particles < 0.00884, e2_sq < 0.00751, tau21_b2 < 0.202 and fewer than 5 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4; lowered for fewer than 25 particles within ΔR < 0.05, for LHA < 0.372, tau21 < 0.347 and girth2 < 0.00961. It falls with lam2 (rank correlation -0.761), tau4 (-0.719), the number of particles (-0.719) and the particle count at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.696). W (0.85), quarks (0.67) and Z (0.52) sit high, gluons (0.12) and tops (0.03) low; it is zero for 52.2% of gluons and 91.0% of tops.
3.role: It raises the W score (+5%) and the Z score (+5%) and lowers the g score (-8%). It does not enter the q or t scores.

4.title: compact core of the hardest particles (width < 0.0096, girth2 of hardest > 0.0046), low D2
4.measures: Raised for width < 0.00961 (its strongest term), girth2 of the 50 hardest particles > 0.00457, girth2 of the 15 hardest > 0.0022 and girth2 of the 20 hardest < 0.0108; lowered for girth2 of the 40 hardest < 0.00803, girth2 of the 50 hardest > 0.00243, pT of the 50 hardest < 1061 GeV and e2 < 0.0436. So it needs a small overall width with the hard particles not all collinear. It falls with D2_b2 (rank correlation -0.696), D2 (-0.691), tau21_b2 (-0.678) and N2 (-0.667) and rises with the mass of the 10 hardest particles (0.657). Z (1.46) and W (1.14) sit highest, then tops (0.78); gluons (0.18) and quarks (0.12) are low, zero for 67.4% and 80.8% of them.
4.role: It lowers the q score (-31%, its largest input) and the g score (-16%), and raises the W score (+6%) and the t score (+4%). It does not enter the Z score.

5.title: pT held in the 50 hardest particles, e2_sq below 0.0079
5.measures: Raised for pT of the 50 hardest particles > 934 GeV (its strongest term) but lowered for log of total pT > 6.91, so it is large when few particles lie beyond the 50 hardest; lowered for e2_sq > 0.00787 and raised for fewer than 64 particles, width > 0.00694 and total pT > 908 GeV with e4 < 5.85e-08. It falls with the particle count at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation -0.611) and the number of particles (-0.604). Z (1.62), W (1.44) and quarks (1.36) sit high, gluons (0.57) and tops (0.31) low; it is zero for 54.5% of tops and 24.5% of gluons.
5.role: It raises the Z score (+17%) and the W score (+15%) and lowers the t score (-13%) and the g score (-8%). It does not enter the q score. Although its weight shares are large, freezing it costs only 0.04 points of accuracy.

6.title: girth2 and e2_sq between about 0.014 and 0.026, or very small lam1
6.measures: Raised for e2_sq < 0.0258 (its strongest term) and lowered for width < 0.00961, girth2 < 0.014, girth2 of the 40 hardest particles < 0.025 and e2 > 0.0154, so it is on for jets of intermediate girth2; for the narrowest jets lam1 < 0.00381, girth2 of the 40 hardest < 0.00884 and lam1 < 0.00767 add back enough to switch it on again, and pT concentration within ΔR < 0.3 (psi_0p3 > 0.985) raises it. It rises with the number of branches removed by soft drop (rank correlation 0.422), tau21_b2 (0.421), tau21 (0.418) and D2_b2 (0.417). Gluons (0.97) and quarks (0.94) sit highest, then tops (0.41), Z (0.13) and W (0.07); it is zero for 91.9% of W and 67.8% of Z jets, whose widths fall between its two ranges.
6.role: It lowers the Z score (-12%) and raises the q score (+4%). It does not enter the g, W or t scores (share +2% in the g score).

7.title: e2_sq and girth2 in a narrow band (0.0079-0.0096), total pT above 1167 GeV
7.measures: Raised for e2_sq < 0.00961 (its strongest term), but the term e2_sq < 0.00961 AND total pT < 1167 GeV pushes it back down, so the rise applies mainly at high pT; lowered for girth2 < 0.00788, girth2 of the 50 hardest particles < 0.00812, girth < 0.0859 and lam1 < 0.00824, so the very narrowest jets are excluded. It rises with eccentricity (rank correlation 0.36) and falls with tau21_b2 (-0.383) and planar flow (-0.36). Z jets sit far above the rest (1.54, AUC 0.91), then gluons (0.23), W (0.11), tops (0.08) and quarks (0.07); it is zero for 12.6% of Z jets, 72.2% of W jets and 91.5% of quarks.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+9%) and lowers the W score (-6%) and the t score (-3%); together with neuron 0 it separates Z from W jets. It does not enter the g or q scores. Freezing it costs 1.32 points of accuracy.

8.title: large girth2 (above 0.014), rising with jet width
8.measures: Raised for girth2 < 0.0259, but the term girth2 < 0.0259 AND log of total pT < 7.14 lowers it by a similar share (-0.191 against +0.174), so below about 1260 GeV total pT the two largely cancel; lowered for girth2 < 0.014, e2_sq < 0.00961 and width < 0.00819, raised for girth2 of the 30 hardest particles < 0.00746 at total pT < 1261 GeV and for tau1 < 0.122. It rises with width, girth2, e2_sq and mass over pT (rank correlation 0.697 each) and with jet mass (0.685). Tops sit far above the rest (3.51, AUC 0.90), then gluons (1.44), quarks (0.57), Z (0.27) and W (0.04); it is zero for 95.1% of W jets and 75.8% of quarks. Its values reach 7.81.
8.role: It lowers the Z score (-26%) and the W score (-24%), the largest input of both, and raises the t score (+6%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

9.title: narrow jets: width below 0.0069 with lam1 between 0.0047 and 0.0073
9.measures: Raised for width < 0.00694 (its strongest term), pT of the 30 hardest particles < 1192 GeV, lam1 > 0.00467 and lam1 < 0.00726, lowered for lam1 > 0.00672, girth2 > 0.0259 and girth2 of the 15 hardest < 0.0268. It falls with the mass of the 40 hardest particles (rank correlation -0.652) and with jet mass (-0.633). Quarks sit highest (2.47, AUC 0.83), then gluons (1.57), tops (0.80), W (0.47) and Z (0.23); it is zero for 81.1% of Z jets.
9.role: It raises the q score (+25%) and the g score (+14%) and lowers the W score (-6%). It does not enter the Z or t scores.
